display.purpose: The one first-viewport headline per page.

label.purpose: Reserved for the wordmark only — never a decorative kicker.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for cards, rows, and list items.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Hover state for cards and the primary sign-in button.

motion.name: ease-premium
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out used for every interactive transition and the page-load rise-in.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: The single authored entrance moment, applied once to a page's outer content wrapper — never cascaded per element.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The accent-filled pill used for the app's one primary action per view (Sign in, Save, Accept, Share).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-foreground); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 12px 20px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(33,29,25,0.04), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(33,29,25,0.12); transition: box-shadow 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), opacity 300ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgba(33,29,25,0.05), 0 16px 40px -16px rgba(33,29,25,0.22); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Quiet destructive action (Decline, Remove, Unshare) — muted, not a shouting filled red.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: var(--danger-muted); color: var(--danger); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: opacity 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { opacity: 0.8; } .ds-btn-danger:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { background: var(--surface-muted); color: var(--muted); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { color: var(--foreground); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Username/duration fields across onboarding, friends, and find-a-time.
components.css: .ds-input { border: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface); border-radius: 12px; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--foreground); outline: none; transition: border-color 200ms; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--danger); }

components.name: Card Row
components.description: A calendar, friend, or event row — the system's one repeating container shape.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 16px; padding: 16px 20px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(33,29,25,0.04), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(33,29,25,0.12); transition: box-shadow 300ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgba(33,29,25,0.05), 0 16px 40px -16px rgba(33,29,25,0.22); }

components.name: Navigation Bar
components.description: Sticky, translucent-blurred header with pill nav links; active route gets a filled pill.
components.html: This weekFind a time
components.css: .ds-nav-link { border-radius: 9999px; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--muted); text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 200ms, color 200ms; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: var(--surface-muted); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-nav-link--active { background: var(--surface-muted); color: var(--foreground); font-weight: 500; }

narrative.overview: Overlap exists to take a small, mundane chore — figuring out when a handful of friends are all free — and handle it with the unhurried confidence of someone who's good at their job and never makes you feel rushed. The system refuses the generic Tailwind-indigo SaaS-dashboard default: no cold slate grays, no scattershot card grids, no kicker labels announcing what a heading already says on its own. It borrows Apple's marketing-page restraint — generous type scale, huge quiet margins, one idea per screen — but stays an Operate-mode tool throughout: nothing here exists to persuade, only to help. Things 3 and Fantastical set the calibration for warmth: this should feel tactile and considered, never clinical.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutrals throughout — ivory and soft charcoal, never cold slate or blue-black
One confident accent (deep pine teal) carrying every primary action and piece of state
One typeface, one scale, no display/body split
Soft dual-layer shadows for depth; no hard offset shadows anywhere
Pill-shaped controls; rounded-corner cards; nothing sharp-edged
One entrance moment per view, never scattered per-element animation

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Deep Pine Teal is the only saturated color in the interface. Danger, success, and warning exist for semantic state only and are deliberately desaturated toward the same warm family.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small tracked label ever sits directly above a heading as a category/eyebrow tag. The wordmark lives in its own corner position instead.

rules.name: The Grows-On-Touch Rule
rules.body: A resting surface uses the Soft shadow; the same surface under hover/focus uses Lifted. Depth is a response to attention, not a static decoration.

dos: Do keep every button pill-shaped and every card/input at the 12px/16px radius steps.
Do route every server-action button through SubmitButton/ConfirmSubmitButton so pending/disabled state is automatic.
Do use Soft shadow at rest and Lifted on hover for any new card or primary button.
Do keep the tracked-uppercase Label treatment to exactly one use — the corner wordmark.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above any heading — this was tried once during the build and reverted.
Don't use a hard offset shadow anywhere — this system is not neobrutalist.
Don't switch to a second typeface or a monospace face for "technical" content.
Don't animate more than one element's entrance per view.
